projects.name: Climate and Clean Air Coalition (CCAC)
projects.description:
An umbrella project/programme with the following components:
1. Develop a national SLCP plan to mainstream SLCP mitigation into existing policy and methane roadmap
2. Enhancing capacity in SLCP Mitigation in Kazakhstan’s coal mining sector (contracting stage)
3. Technical expert assistance to strengthen capacity of government entities to identify opportunities for enhancing short-lived climate pollutant (SLCP) action ahead of the 2025 Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) update
4. National Cooling Action Plan (NCAP) & a Methane Mitigation Strategy in Agriculture
5. Develop a methane mitigation strategy for Kazakhstan’s Agricultural Sector
6. Building Climate-Resilient Cities and Communities in the Republic of Kazakhstan

projects.name: Institutional Support to the Astana Civil Service Hub, Phase 4
projects.description: The project's overall goal is to contribute to effective, transparent, and accountable governance and improved public service delivery in the region and beyond, through civil service excellence and regional cooperation. Since 2013, the ACSH operates as a multilateral and networking platform promoting supporting public service excellence, by assisting the efforts of the participating countries’ governments – particularly those in the immediate region – in building institutional and human capacity to cope with contemporary challenges and issues through three main pillars: (i) partnerships and networking; (ii) capacity building and peer-to-peer learning; and (iii) research and knowledge creation and management. It is worth noting that all ACSH activities are shaped by a flexible demand-driven agenda, which has proved its relevance in regional and international development cooperation over the years. The quality of its work has been highly acclaimed by the United Nations and its sister agencies, as well as by the European Union, and the Organisation for Economic Development and Cooperation and by many participating countries. The vision and mandate of this fourth phase of the project is to continue contributing to the establishment of modern, effective, efficient, and sustainable governance, public administration, and civil service systems in its participating countries and beyond, which meet society’s expectations for responsive, accountable, and transparent public institutions; in congruence with the SDG 16 and 17 objectives.

projects.name: Conservation and Sustainable Management of Key Globally Important Ecosystems for Multiple Benefits (Global Policy Centre on Resilient Ecosystems - 2021)
projects.description: The Project is aimed to improve the conservation and management of forest resources and adjacent grassland, floodplain and desert ecosystems, which are valuable for biodiversity conservation, land resources and welfare of local communities. The Project also focuses on promoting the gender equality and women empowerment as relevant and possible within the Project. In this direction, the Project will address the challenges of sustainable use of natural resources by promoting innovative gender-responsible solutions based on improved capacity, new knowledge, new opportunities, increased participation of women in the development and implementation of effective methods and approaches of sustainable forest and rangeland management, etc. To achieve the Project goal and reduce certain threats and barriers, the project structure involves 3 Components. Geographically, the target project areas coincide with the key biodiversity areas (KBA) identified in Kazakhstan, including the mountain, tugai and saxaul forests. The listed ecosystems, among which the mountain ecosystems are the main habitat of snow leopard, are forming part of 3 administrative oblasts, where the Project is planned to be implemented: East Kazakhstan oblast  (mountain areas of Altai and Saur-Tarbagatai), Almaty oblast (Zhongar Alatau, Northern and Central Tien Shan, floodplain forests of the Charyn and Ili rivers, and Pribalkhash saxaul forests), and South Kazakhstan oblast (mountain ecosystems of Western Tien Shan and floodplain forests of SyrDarya river)

projects.name: Derisking renewable energy investment
projects.description:
The objective of the project is to encourage private sector investment in renewable energy in Kazakhstan to achieve the objectives of the “Kazakhstan 2030” and “Kazakhstan 2050” strategies for renewable energy.
The project targets both large-scale and small-scale renewable energy sources. The ultimate goal of this project is to achieve the transformation of the energy market in Kazakhstan through a significant increase in the scale of the use of renewable energy sources in the field of electricity generation, from 0.77% to 10% - the share of RES by 2030, which is a 10-fold increase in electricity generation based on RES with the assistance of the project.
In terms of large-scale renewable energy sources, the project will help promote Kazakhstan as a prime target for foreign investment. Technologies will include wind power and photovoltaic solar power (PV).
For small-scale renewable energy sources, the project will stimulate investment in "Renewable energy sources for Urban Life", small-scale renewable energy sources for grid systems, intended for urban population and enterprises; and in RES for Rural Life, small-scale renewable energy sources for both grid and off-grid systems for farms and rural SMEs. Technologies may include solar PV (on rooftops), solar water heating and small-scale wind energy.

projects.name: Nationally Appropriate Mitigation Actions for Low-Carbon Urban Development
projects.description: The project supports the development and implementation of climate change mitigation actions (NAMA) in Kazakhstan's urban sector. Through infrastructure investments, capacity-building, and technical assistance, it aims to reduce greenhouse gas emissions while enhancing urban services and citizens' quality of life. Aligned with UNDP’s Strategic Plan, the project focuses on accelerating the transition to renewable energy and green recovery. It includes components to enhance municipal planning, strengthen institutional structures, facilitate financing, and pilot urban NAMA in Nur-Sultan. The project will also harmonize with national emission reduction efforts, including monitoring and verification systems, aiming for direct emission reductions of 370,000 tons of CO2-eq. and indirect reductions from 1 to 5 million tons of CO2-eq.

projects.name: Phase 2: Supporting the Economic Empowerment of Afghan Women through Education and Training in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan
projects.description:
The Action represents an expansion of an ongoing EUR 2 million trilateral cooperation programme between the European Union, Afghanistan, and Central Asia. Like the ongoing programme, it aims at building resilience and promoting the academic, economic and social empowerment of women in Afghanistan especially vulnerable women living in challenging conditions by enhancing their capabilities, employability and future prospects through education and training in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and, within the context of this Action, Kyrgyzstan.
Phase 2 of the programme focuses on training of specialists in Agriculture/Agribusiness, Engineering/Construction, Marketing and ICT. Apart from promoting academic, economic and social empowerment of women in Afghanistan, the action will help to strengthen capacity of receiving institutions in Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Kyrgyzstan to manage learning mobility programmes in interaction with UNDP and address gender inequalities in higher education and TVET.
The action is intended as a logical continuation of the ongoing project and aims to further facilitate the development of a sustainable system of academic exchange that will allow women from Afghanistan to benefit from higher education opportunities in Central Asia also beyond the project lifetime.

projects.name: Creation of conditions for the reintroduction of the Turan tiger and assistance in the preservation of natural, historical and cultural objects of the Ulytau mountain range
projects.description:
The Project is aimed at creating a sustainable base for reintroduction of tigers in historical habitats, spanning the Ile-Balkhash SNR, conservating the natural, historical and cultural heritage of Ulytau mountain range and adjacent territories, and promoting the tourist sites in this unique region. The Project's main results will be a comprehensive improvement of ecosystems along the Ile river delta and the Southern Balkhash region, strengthening Ile-Balkhash SNR and Ulytau SNNP (which is being created), developing a PAs network and tourism in Ulytau region, raising the level of environmental awareness by population and informing all stakeholders, creating a basis for joint ecosystems management with the project sites with benefits for biodiversity conservation and local communities. The
project will contribute to the enhancement of women’s role in the restoration and conservation activities, extensively applying gendered approach during implementation phase through capacity building, meaningful participation of women in decision-making and monitoring as well as inclusion of their needs and interest in project design.balkhash saxaul forests), and South Kazakhstan oblast (mountain ecosystems of Western Tien Shan and floodplain forests of SyrDarya river).

projects.name: Creating conditions for the attraction of investors in energy efficiency in Kazakhstan
projects.description:
The Project aims to advance energy efficiency of buildings, infrastructure, and other facilities in Kazakhstan by attracting investment from private investors, banks and international financial institutions via the design, piloting, and development of a partial credit guarantee scheme supporting bank loans to small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) that have limited access to credit due to their lack of suitable collateral.
By facilitating investment into this sector, the Project will stimulate economic growth and sustainability among SMEs, thus creating and preserving jobs and accelerating economic recovery from the COVID-19 crisis.  The Project will also help to fulfil Kazakhstan’s national strategic goals for decreasing energy intensity of the GDP.
Toward these goals, the Project will create and pilot the loan guarantee scheme, conduct supporting activity in training and monitoring, and scale up the loan guarantee fund on the basis of initial results.  Eligible businesses will include providers of energy-saving services and equipment; energy end-users seeking to upgrade efficiency of facilities and energy systems; and intermediaries (micro-finance organizations, leasing companies, factoring companies) that finance eligible businesses or projects mentioned above.

projects.name: Seventh Operational Phase of the GEF Small Grants Programme in Kazakhstan
projects.description: The project aims to empower local communities and organizations to enhance socio-ecological resilience and sustainable livelihoods across seven target landscapes, benefitting both local and global environments. It will achieve this by improving community-based capacities for ecosystem resilience through resource management planning and promoting the adoption of energy-efficient and renewable energy technologies to reduce greenhouse gas emissions. Focused on steppe and desert landscapes, the project will deliver cost-effective investments, processes, and tools within specific geographic areas. By fostering synergies among community interventions, it aims to maximize impacts and results on the landscape through cumulative efforts. Leveraging additional funds from various sources, including government and private sector initiatives, the project aligns closely with government priorities at both national and regional levels, facilitating collaboration with existing programs.

projects.name: Equipping learners in Kazakhstan with skills and competencies to promote sustainable development and engage with the world as responsible global citizens
projects.description:
The overall purpose of UNESCO Almaty's support to Kazakhstan is to enhance education quality and relevance by focusing on functional literacy, critical thinking, and transversal skills among learners. This involves reviewing and analyzing national policies and curricula, enhancing curriculum content, and developing learning materials on Education for Sustainable Development (ESD), Global Citizenship Education (GCED), Media and Information Literacy (MIL), and healthy lifestyles.

Key actions include:

Conducting mapping studies and analysis to integrate ESD, GCED, and MIL into national education standards.
Reviewing and revising the curriculum to integrate 21st-century competencies and ESD topics.
Developing the ESD-2030 Country Initiative, a national plan for mainstreaming ESD and implementing SDG 4.7.
Supporting the review of teacher training programs and developing a new concept for the teacher training system.
Introducing greening education standards and reviewing climate change education.
Developing learning and teaching materials on ESD, climate change education, and healthy lifestyles to support the learning process and equip learners with necessary skills for sustainable development.

projects.name: Training and supporting teachers in Kazakhstan to improve learning outcomes and address the changes brought forth by the digital and artificial intelligence (AI) transformation and the COVID-19 crisis
projects.description: Overall purpose is to address learning loss due to the Covid-19 crisis and improve of learning outcomes in Kazakhstan through the provision of policy support on teachers, training and supporting teachers and developing teaching and instructional materials. This will help teachers to provide adequate remediation and deliver different modalities of learning in order to address learning loss and improve learning outcomes.  UNESCO will provide support in building capacity of teachers in the fields of ESD, ICT in education, including cyber safety and healthy lifestyles. With the support of Ministry of Foreign Affairs of Kazakhstan, teachers from rural schools will be supported to create professional learning circles and develop non-positional leadership with the purpose of addressing the quality of learning outcomes.

projects.name: Promotion of sustainable food systems and improved ecosystems services in Northern Kazakhstan Landscape
projects.description: The project, part of the global GEF Impact Program on Food Systems, Land Use, and Restoration (FOLUR), aims to promote efficient land management technologies and green value chains to reduce degradation in the Northern KZ Landscape. It will support Integrated Landscape Management policies and capacities to transform land use practices and prevent ecosystem degradation. Key components include establishing a cooperative platform with wheat exporters and retail companies, diversifying and improving management of croplands, introducing agro-environmental incentives, and restoring pasture land. Additionally, it will establish a network of high-nature value ecosystems and finance reforestation pilots and restoration demos for dryland forests and degraded lake and wetland ecosystems. The project will also facilitate knowledge exchange, vocational and academic training programs, and advocacy for sustainable food production and conservation.

projects.name: Institutionalization of adaptation planning and integration of climate risks into Kazakhstan’s development planning processes to enable implementation of adaptation measures as part of coherent National Adaptation Planning (NAP) policies
projects.description:
The proposed readiness project in the Republic of Kazakhstan addresses the urgent need to enhance resilience against the impacts of climate change. Recognizing the President's call for action, the Government supports the National Adaptation Plan (NAP) processes to integrate climate adaptation into policies, especially related to NDC implementation and decarbonization.
Focused on four priority sectors—agriculture, forestry, water management, and civil protection/disaster risk reduction – the project aims to establish clear mandates, coordination mechanisms, and standard procedures for climate adaptation at both national and sub-national levels. It seeks to provide decision-makers with climate services, enabling a comprehensive understanding of climate impacts and adaptation options. The project also aims to empower experts in the identified sectors to integrate climate risks into standard planning and budgeting procedures. Objectives include strengthening governance and institutional coordination, producing evidence for impactful adaptation solutions, catalyzing private sector engagement, and increasing adaptation finance. Emphasis will be placed on utilizing existing planning and budgeting processes for sustainable funding. Beneficiaries encompass key government ministries, decision-makers at various levels, business planners, and climate and sectoral experts, including women and vulnerable groups, contributing to a climate-resilient development pathway.
projects.outcome: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.

Bilateral meetings with key stakeholders addressed gaps in legislation hindering refugees' access to social services, employment, healthcare, and education. Refugee components were included in the 2nd Voluntary National Review under SDG 10 and SDG 16, emphasizing equal access to socio-economic rights and protection for refugee children. Recommendations for refugee education were made in the UN National Consultations report, to be presented at the Transforming Education Summit in September 2022.

UNHCR collaborated with national academic institutions to provide higher education scholarship opportunities for Ukrainian asylum-seekers and extended the scope to all refugees, aligning with the Global Compact on Refugees. Additionally, 9 refugee youth received DAFI scholarships to study at universities and technical colleges in Kazakhstan."

projects.name: Lifecycle Management of Pesticides and Disposal of POPs Pesticides in CA countries and Turkey
projects.description:
GCP /SEC/011/GFF “Lifecycle Management of Pesticides and Disposal of POPs Pesticides in CA countries and Turkey” project is a regional project in Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan, Turkiye. The project objective is to reduce Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs) releases from obsolete pesticide stockpiles and contaminated sites and strengthen the capacity for the sound management of pesticides. Specific objectives of each component are to: safely destroy up to 900 tonnes of POPs and obsolete pesticides and remediate a pesticide-contaminated site (Component 1); strengthen the institutional and regulatory framework for managing pesticides through their life cycle (Component 2); and increase the successful uptake of alternatives to chemical pesticides on key crops (Component 3). These three components are supported by a horizontal project management, Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) and communication component (Component 4) which will inform project execution decisions and create the necessary conditions for beneficiary knowledge and participation in project activities.
The project dates: 15-Oct-2018 - 31-Dec-2024 
The project document was signed by the Government of Kazakhstan in August 2021.

projects.name: Improving the technical potential of the State Revenue Committee in Kazakhstan
projects.description:
In response to a request from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is initiating a project to enhance the technical capabilities of the State Revenue Committee of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Kazakhstan, by the procurement and delivery of border equipment. This project is funded by the Governments of the United Kingdom and the Kingdom of the Netherlands, along with the Delegation of the European Union in Kazakhstan.
The State Revenue Committee of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Kazakhstan is currently exploring methods to strengthen and improve the mechanisms for controlling the movement of goods subject to export control along the Kazakhstan-Russian and Kazakhstan-Kyrgyz borders.
This initiative is a collaborative effort between Kazakhstan and its European partners to ensure compliance with the sanctions’ regime for High Priority List and dual-use goods transported across the state borders of the Republic of Kazakhstan. UNDP will utilize the contributions to purchase customs equipment, specific types of equipment will be determined by the donors in consultation with the State Revenue Committee of the Ministry of Finance of the Republic of Kazakhstan.

projects.description: The UNIDO regional demonstration project for the coordinated management of ozone-depleting substances (ODS) and persistent organic pollutants (POPs) disposal in Belarus, Kazakhstan and Armenia aims to demonstrate environmentally sound approaches to the collection and destruction of these hazardous substances. By addressing multiple focal areas, the project supports participating countries in fulfilling their obligations under the Stockholm Convention and the Montreal Protocol, while strengthening national capacities for the safe and sustainable management of ODS and POPs.

projects.name: Biodiversity finance initiative – BIOFIN, Extended Phase II
projects.description: BIOFIN supports countries with a methodology that provides innovative steps to measure current biodiversity expenditures, assess financial needs, identify the most suitable finance solutions, and provides guidance on how to implement these solutions to achieve their national biodiversity target. The 2nd phase of BIOFIN in Kazakhstan will be built on the lessons learned from the 1st phase and will aim to test six finance solutions: (1) subsidizing game breeding, (2) creating a basis for certification in the field of ecotourism, (3) capacity building of protected areas to improve financing, (4) biodiversity offsets, (5) carbon offsetting through an internal emission trading system (ETS) and (6) attracting foreign investment to implement projects to absorb greenhouse gases by forest ecosystems. The Phase II aims to establish the institutional and legal basis that will allow mobilizing financial resources for biodiversity through new financial solutions. Implementation of new finance solutions will be based on changing existing and preparing new legal standards, testing, studying the experience of other countries, approaches, capacity building of industry experts, providing extensive information on the problems and possibilities of biodiversity financing. The project also aims to highlight the key role of women in the conservation and sustainable use of biological diversity, as well as the need for the full involvement of women at all levels of decision-making by mainstreaming gender issues into new financial decisions.

projects.name: Advocating social and economic rights for the refugees, asylum seekers and stateless persons
projects.description:
As part of a working group on formulating the Migration Policy for 2023-27 and Social Code, UNHCR supported the Government by providing its technical expertise and recommendations for development of a Migration Policy for 2023-2027 and Social Code to enhance the national legal framework on asylum, refugee integration, extending their socio-economic rights including access to social protection services and allowance and facilitating naturalization. In the framework of Joint work plan with Ministry of Labour and Social Protection, UNHCR conducted sequence of capacity building workshops for representatives of the Ministry and local executive bodies, and representatives of national refugee status determination commission.  
Bilateral meetings were conducted with line Ministries (MLSP, MoH, MoJ, MoEd), Members of the Parliament, Human Rights Ombudsman and other stakeholders, where the current situation of refugees, asylum-seekers and stateless persons in Kazakhstan, existing gaps in national legislation which hinder them from having effective access to social protection, employment, healthcare, education services, and necessary actions to be taken by the Government to promote and ensure the full realization of all human rights for all persons without discrimination in order to meet Kazakhstan’s obligations under international conventions were discussed. UNHCR recommendations were reflected in the Kazakhstan’s Human Rights action plan for 2022-2024. 
The refugee components were included in the 2nd Voluntary National Review (VNR) under SDG 10 “Granting access to basic socio-economic rights to refugees and asylum-seekers on an equal basis with permanently residing foreigners during their stay in Kazakhstan” and under SDG 16 “Ensuring the protection of the rights and interests of refugee and stateless children, ensuring security and access to social and educational services”. 

The situation of refugees in Kazakhstan along with challenges faced by them were submitted in the framework of UN Human Rights commissions (CERD and CAT) with recommendations to the Government of Kazakhstan to facilitate socio-economic integration and naturalization of refugees in line with international standards.
projects.outcome: Output 1.1.1: Improved capacity of authorities at national and sub-national level to provide effective social protection programmes and social services, including COVID-19 related services, with the focus on the most vulnerable groups.

projects.name: Sustainable development: bridging local disparities for newly created regions
projects.description:
This Initiation Plan is aimed at detecting region's development priorities of the two newly created regions of Kazakhstan (Ulytau and Abay) to form the ground for full-scale regional development programme aimed at eliminating uneven development at the regional level, improving the quality of life of the population and promoting progress in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals in the regions of the country.
Identifying the regions’ development potential and growth points will be done through testing the best global and domestic practices (including by transferring successful cases from one region to another) to demonstrate the most optimal and economically feasible solutions, including on the basis of advanced water and energy saving technologies, use of environmentally friendly materials, technologies and knowledge to improve labour productivity, and production of high value-added products. Specific emphasis will be put on development of technical solutions that support planning, prevention, preparedness and response to flood emergencies in the regions.
Additionally, IP will support the Government in preparation for the Voluntary National Review on the SDGs in 2025 to conduct a comprehensive review of Kazakhstan progress towards the SDGs, SDG 5 being one of top priority SDGs, identify gaps and challenges, and develop strategies and action plans to accelerate progress towards achieving the goals.

 Conducting assessments and designing renovations for laboratories and construction of a new facility in Turkestan with SMART and green technologies.
 Renovating the National Research Center for Problems of Especially Dangerous Infections (NPCSEM) and modernizing sanitary and quarantine checkpoints.

Contribute to coordination of effort in assessing national financial gaps using the Integrated National Financing Framework (INFF) methodology and ongoing Development Finance Assessments and stimulating regional exchange of best practices. 3. Establish tools that can support evidence-based policymaking and track SDG progress and contribution (outcome) of the EU regional programmes in SDG achievement, focusing on policies with transboundary impact, including environment, water and biodiversity, trade, and social development. 4. Promote the use of innovative practices that can visualize key SDG progress showing possible trends and hotspots in Central Asia countries and communication.

In this context, UNESCO will provide its support to Kazakhstan with development of policy recommendations, learning and teaching materials as well as capacity building in such areas as ICT in education, using AI in education, ensuring cyber safety and cyber security. UNHCR recommendations were reflected in the Kazakhstan’s Human Rights action plan for 2022-2024. 
The refugee components were included in the 2nd Voluntary National Review (VNR) under SDG 10 “Granting access to basic socio-economic rights to refugees and asylum-seekers on an equal basis with permanently residing foreigners during their stay in Kazakhstan” and under SDG 16 “Ensuring the protection of the rights and interests of refugee and stateless children, ensuring security and access to social and educational services”. 
The situation of refugees in Kazakhstan along with challenges faced by them were submitted in the framework of UN Human Rights commissions (CERD and CAT) with recommendations to the Government of Kazakhstan to facilitate socio-economic integration and naturalization of refugees in line with international standards.

This project covers twelve countries situated in three geographical regions, i.e., in the Caucasus, and in Asia and the Pacific, which have taken some steps towards the digitalisation of their government operations and processes and for the delivery of public services to business and citizens, however in a varying degree. Moreover, most of them have also embraced the notion of digital transformation and of digital governance in their development strategies, although much still needs to be done towards their goal for digital transformation; incorporating the latest digital technologies, i.e., evidence-based policy formulation and implementation by harnessing abundant “big data”, or for the provision of proactive, efficient, and effective public services digitally.
Hence, this project – fully recognising the value of digital transformation and of digital governance – aims at further developing the capacities of public servants at different levels of government by transferring knowledge and experience enabling them to implement initiatives that will advance digital transformation and digital governance in their countries. It is expected that such knowledge and experience sharing will assist the participating countries to further develop policies initiatives that will allow them to establish data-driven public sectors for evidence-based policy making and implementation, and to introduce digital open governments that are proactive and user-driven resulting to efficient and effective public service provision and an increase of trust in government. Ultimately, utilising digitalisation for shaping public governance outcomes will be beneficial for their citizens.

projects.name: Climate Promise Kazakhstan – From Pledge to Impact
projects.description:
This Project is part of the global UNDP’s flagship initiative, the Climate Promise: From Pledge to Impact - Leveraging the Climate Promise to turn enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (eNDC) into ambitious climate action.
The project has been initiated as a response to the country's request for NDC Partnership. This project aims to support national efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, aligning with commitments such as the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and the Carbon Neutral Strategy. It involves developing a comprehensive tool and methodology to evaluate the impact of national programs and policies on GHG emissions, as well as building capacity among stakeholders to effectively use these tools.
The project also focuses on establishing measurable emission reduction outcomes, including long-term targets and interim milestones for key sectors. Sector-specific reduction pathways will be developed based on projections and scenarios, identifying programs and projects that can contribute to emissions reduction. Additionally, the project includes a social and gender impact assessment of the Carbon Neutral Strategy to ensure an equitable transition, along with the development of legislation and regulations to strengthen waste management practices and reduce sectoral emissions.

projects.name: Flood Control Using Integrated Dam Management System
projects.description:
The flood situation in 2024 was an unprecedented event. Frozen soil, sudden temperature rise and rainfall in conjunction with a considerable snow layer resulted in extremely high flows in the north and west of Kazakhstan. Many rivers experienced all-time high water levels and flood defence structures could not cope with the extreme flood volumes. The flood inundated large areas including settlements and agricultural zones and Aktobe was one of the hardest-hit cities in Kazakhstan.
This unprecedented flood revealed that preparedness, as part of efficient flood management, was not developed as it was supposed to be. The flood early warning systems to provide sufficient lead time did not exist. Specifically, dams did not have early warning systems which means preparation and foresighted flood operation are either not in place or just based on estimations and experiences of dam operators. However, the operators lack experience in addressing the increase in flow intensity, flow variability and speed floods developed in recent years due to climate change.
All in all, dams need urgent modernization in terms of three pillars: (1) Dam integrity; (2) Monitoring and dam surveillance; (3) Operation to enhance the flood management strategy in Kazakhstan, protect downstream riparians and ensure the full potential of flood attenuation of dams. Therefore, dams must be embedded into the national flood management concept of Kazakhstan as best as possible requiring the enhancement of early warning, dam monitoring, the rehabilitation of outdated structures and an update of operation rules.
The project aims to enhance flood resilience in Kazakhstan by strengthening dam safety and flood preparedness, directly supporting the disaster risk reduction and water priority sectors outlined in Kazakhstan's updated Nationally Determined Contributions (NDC). The updated NDC includes a dedicated chapter on climate change adaptation, emphasizing the importance of water resources management and disaster risk reduction as national adaptation priorities. This project aligns with these goals by improving infrastructure and preparedness measures to mitigate flood risks. Additionally, it complements the UNDP's ongoing initiative to integrate national adaptation plans into regional development strategies, ensuring a unified and comprehensive approach to climate resilience and sustainable development throughout Kazakhstan.
projects.outcome: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.

The project will facilitate Kazakhstan in improving emission data, conducting focused research, and enhancing technical capacity and institutions for both mitigation and adaptation. projects.name: Establishing HIV-1 Recent Infection Surveillance among Persons Newly Diagnosed with HIV Infection in KZ
projects.description:
GAM Report.  The UNAIDS office provided crucial technical assistance to Kazakhstan, supporting the timely submission of 80 key indicators for the Global AIDS Monitoring Reports. They enhanced the capabilities of 50 epidemiologists and 20 lab specialists across 20 AIDS Centers, improving their capacity to track progress toward the 95-95-95 targets. This effort aligns with Kazakhstan's commitment to the UN Political Declaration to end AIDS by 2030, showcasing tangible progress and contributing to the global fight against HIV/AIDS. 
Establishing HIV-1 Recent Infection Surveillance among Persons Newly Diagnosed with HIV Infection in Kazakhstan. The UNAIDS office played a pivotal role in aiding the Kazakh Scientific Center for Dermatology and Infection Diseases, under the Ministry of Health of Kazakhstan in enhancing the capabilities of staff across 20 AIDS regional centers in Kazakhstan. The focus was on implementing HIV Recency testing, an innovative methodology crucial for identifying recent HIV infections and tracing potential routes of transmission. Recent infections are more prevalent among urban residents (21%), with sex workers (25%) and men who have sex with men (22%) showing the highest proportions among key populations. A training workshop equipped 40 specialists from 20 regional and city HIV prevention centers to utilize the Spectrum program for subnational data preparation. Preliminary evaluation data from 20 centers were processed in Spectrum programme. Insights from these efforts are instrumental in translating data into impactful HIV prevention actions. Three Technical Working Group meetings conducted involving the AIDS service NGOs, community of People Living with HIV, and national/international organizations, focusing on the 2023-2026 HIV Roadmap. Also, staff members from the Kazakhstan Scientific Centre of Dermatology and Infectious Diseases contributed to the Regional HIV Assessment Workshop in Chisinau, Moldova, held from February 27 to March 3.

projects.name: Develop and test sustainable models to expand children and young people’s access to skills training and opportunities for participation in social innovation and entrepreneurship.
projects.description:
2021: UNICEF, in partnership with the Ministry of Labor and Social Protection of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Ministry of Labor and Social Development of the Republic of Kazakhstan and the NGO “Community of Youth Workers”, is piloting a sustainable model for developing the skills of adolescents and youth for employment, social innovation and entrepreneurship. The program is based on the internationally recognized Upshift approach. In Kazakhstan, it started in 2020 under the name Samgau, combining online training to strengthen skills for life and employment, hands-on workshops on innovation, mentoring and small grants to pilot developed solutions. The program is presented in the form of modules that can be adapted in different conditions and contexts (general education and special schools, innovation laboratories, children's and youth centers, etc.).

In 2021, UNICEF, with the support of the Ministry of Education and Science of the Republic of Kazakhstan and regional education departments, implemented this program in 10 rural schools and 5 regional youth centers in Aktobe, Atyrau, East Kazakhstan, Karaganda and Kyzylorda regions.
At present, the next stage of expanding the program in other schools and youth centers of the country is being prepared by selecting schools and centers with local authorities.

projects.name: Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) Phase II Implementation of Component I in Kazakhstan
projects.description:
UNDP KZ and the Global Policy Centre on Resilient Ecosystems and Desertification (GC-RED) in Nairobi are collaborating to implement the Biodiversity and Ecosystem Services Network (BES-Net) in KZ. The project aims to formalize partnerships between scientists, policymakers, and practitioners to enhance synergy for sustainable conservation and management of biodiversity and ecosystem services (BES) in Kazakhstan. Recognizing the disproportionate vulnerability of women to climate change and the importance of their empowerment for environmental conservation, the project integrates gender-sensitive actions throughout its design and implementation. The collaboration focuses on four main components:

1. Creating a shared vision and collaboration model among science, policy, and practice communities for sustainable BES conservation and management.
2. Improving access to policy-relevant BES evidence and utilization of new knowledge through national ecosystem assessments.
3. Strengthening multi-sectoral stakeholder dialogue and networks at the regional level to analyze IPBES products and translate relevant messages into concrete decisions and actions.
4. Enhancing BES knowledge sharing through increased generation, dissemination, and communication of resources among science, policy, and practice communities.

projects.name: Integrated Policy Strategies and Regional Policy Coordination for Resilient, Green and Transformative Development: Supporting Selected Asian BRI Partner Countries to Achieve 2030 Sustainable Development Agenda
projects.description:
Project countries: Kazakhstan, Malaysia, Pakistan, Türkiye.
Project Manager: Gul Unal, Senior Economist, Division on Globalization and Development Strategies, UNCTAD (gul.unal@un.org)
Objective: To strengthen regional partnership and national capacities of developing integrated policy strategies in selected countries to achieve the resilient, green and transformative development for 2030 Agenda.

The project comprises three phases:
Phase I: Research collaboration with experts from the project countries to understand their constraints in achieving resilient, green, and transformative development. Research will also focus on China's policies since 2015 for economic resilience and high-quality development (HQD).
Phase II: Development of tailored integrated green development strategies with national partners, addressing capacity gaps through peer-learning with China (South-South Cooperation).
Phase III: Establishment of the Asian Green Development Partnership Network (AGDPN) based on the outputs of Phases I and II, facilitating regional policy coordination and economic cooperation.

projects.name: Member State capacity to effectively apply international labour standards, develop and implement policies focused on improving labour and social conditions at workplaces in specific sectors.
projects.description: Mining represents an important source of income worldwide and the influence of the mining and metallurgical industry (MMI) on the macroeconomic performance of the country is substantial. However, the largest number of those working in unfavourable working conditions in all aspects falls on the mining industry of the country. For the last decade there were over 150 fatalities in mining sector and over 600 workers were injured. To address the challenges with occupational hazards, deceases and mortality as well as to bring the national legislation in compliance with international labour standards, ILO jointly with national tripartite constituents in Kazakhstan signed the Roadmap on decent work promotion in June 2024. As part of this roadmap implementation, the national project "Enhancing Occupational Safety and Health through Social Dialogue in Mining Sector in Kazakhstan" was officially launched in December 2024. The project contributes to strengthening fundamental principles and rights at work in mining sector by enhancing application of core ILO Conventions on freedom of association (C87), collective bargaining (C98), and occupational safety & health (OSH) (C155 and C187) as well as Labour Inspection Conventions (C81 and 129). The project anticipates the ILO support to the government in addressing compliance gaps identified by the ILO Committee of Experts and in preparation to ratification of C102 on minimum social standards, C176 on safety in mines and C190 on prevention and countering violence and harrassment at workplace.

projects.name: Strengthening Resilience to Violent Extremism in Asia (STRIVE Asia): a joint EU-UN partnership
projects.description:
“Strengthening Resilience to Violent Extremism in Asia (STRIVE Asia): a joint EU-UN partnership” project seeks to contribute to preventing and countering violent extremism (P/CVE) in Central, South and Southeast Asia through a whole of society/multi-stakeholder approach including governments, security actors, civil society and the private sector. The specific objective is that key Government (executive and its security agencies and legislative bodies, where appropriate) and non-Government actors are better prepared to contribute to P/CVE objectives in targeted regions and countries.
In Central Asia, including Kazakhstan, the Project focuses on strengthening local resilience of at-risk communities through the support of community-led initiatives in the P/CVE area.

projects.name: Undertake an analysis of financial literacy and remittance management policy and practices in CA countries and the Russian Federation (RF), including technical capacity to utilise digital remittances.
projects.description: The research targeted at remittance senders (migrants in the Russian Federation and Kazakhstan) and remittance recipients (families of migrants in Kyrgyzstan, Tajikistan and Uzbekistan). A total of 500 migrants who were working in the Russian Federation were interviewed (100 from Kyrgyzstan, 125 from Tajikistan, 225 Uzbekistan, and 50 from Kazakhstan). In Kazakhstan, 400 migrants were interviewed (50 from Kyrgyzstan, 50 from Tajikistan, and 300 from Uzbekistan). For recipients of remittances, we interviewed 700 respondents in total (150 in Kyrgyzstan, 250 in Tajikistan, 300 in Uzbekistan, and 100 in Kazakhstan).

projects.name: Provide expert support to the Government on regional and national levels on managing human mobility as an adaptation strategy in the context of climate change with a special focus on mountain areas in Kazakhstan
projects.description:
The project completed a lLongitudinal/ panel study on migration and climate change in Ecuador, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan to strengthen the evidence base on human mobility in contexts of disasters, environmental degradation, and climate change from the perspective of in mountainous areas from the perspective of in Kazakhstan, with special attention to high mountains. The project built an evidence base for the development of future MECC policy and programming in Kazakhstan based on the current policy and national legislation on the MECC nexus and drafted an inventory of relevant laws, policies, and strategies in Kazakhstan to ensure the cross-cutting nature of both migration and climate change are integrated in the analysis was discussed with national partners, and final recommendations developed.
2024:The longitudinal study on human mobility in the context of climate change in the mountainous areas of the Almaty oblast in Kazakhstan demonstrated the complex and multifaceted impacts of environmental and climate hazards on households in the mountain areas. As per the research results, rising temperatures, earthquakes, blizzards, strong winds, and abnormal heat and cold conditions put pressure on the local population, affecting physical safety, water security, and mental well-being. Despite the difficult environmental conditions in the study area this year, residents prefer to stay in their communities.
projects.outcome: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.

projects.description: 2021: A media campaign is being prepared to empower people living with HIV (adults and young people/adolescents) to adhere to HIV treatment and reduce HIV-related stigma and discrimination including self-stigma. For this, a media company called “7 Media” was selected through a competitive bidding. It first reviewed similar campaigns previously implemented in Kazakhstan and other countries and suggested to move away from traditional short videos demonstrated on TV and in digital media. Instead of one or several public service announcements, 7 Media developed a script for a single 20-minute feature film having consultations with people living with HIV, health professionals, opinion leaders and celebrities. By the end of 2021, the film was shot. After post-production refinements, soundtrack recording, poster and teaser production, the film will be released and heavily promoted on popular websites and communities in social media networks. The tentative launch date of the film is 14 February 2022 and it's expected to reach at least 100,000 views by 31 March 2022.

projects.name: Research on awareness of young people of HIV and its prevention to further develop appropriate campaigns on a country-level
projects.description:
Activity: an assessment of young people’s HIV/SRHR awareness level, information needs, media consumption and available services will be conducted; 
strategies for effective HIV prevention will be devised and shared with key stakeholders. Using ICT-powered solutions along with content in Kazakh language will be prioritized to maximize the number of people reached, especially among Kazakh-speaking underserved audiences. Based on the research results, one HIV prevention/SRHR promotion strategy (a media campaign) targeting young key populations will be implemented jointly with local partners to reach out over 50,000 people by the end of 2025. 
Expected results: The project will enhance national capacity for effective stewardship of HIV prevention responses for young people including key young populations by suggesting evidence-informed approaches for HIV communication strategies addressing the needs of the priority target audiences. 
Context: Since 2018, no national assessments of young people’s HIV and SRHR awareness and behavior have been conducted. As advised by the national UBRAF proposal review committee, young people’s HIV/SRHR awareness level, information needs, media consumption and available services will be analyzed to inform the HIV prevention activities and effectively address such barriers as low awareness level, stigma and self-stigma, harmful gender norms.

projects.name: Development of project management system in the activities of state bodies
projects.description:
The Government of Kazakhstan is actively working to introduce modern project management approaches required in the new realities. The legislative basis for the implementation of project activities in public administration has been formed. The implementation of the project-network model in public administration is envisaged at three levels: portfolio level – at the level of the Government and the Presidential Administration of the Republic of Kazakhstan; program level – at the level of central and local executive bodies; project level – direct implementation of projects by creating project teams and their activities.
The main aim of the project is to improve the quality of public administration and the extent to which key aspects of project management are embedded in the activities of state bodies.
One of the key objectives of the project is to increase the motivation of project staff to develop professional competencies and introduce best practices in project management and to develop project maturity in the country as a whole.

projects.name: Enhancing women's legal protection, promoting gender equality, and ensuring their full participation in the socio-political life of the country for 2025–2027
projects.description:
Project  “Enhancing women's legal protection, promoting gender equality, and ensuring their full participation in the socio-political life of the country for 2025–2027”. The project aims to advance gender equality and strengthen women’s empowerment in Kazakhstan by addressing systemic challenges and leveraging existing opportunities. It responds to barriers to gender equality in Kazakhstan and addresses the need for more coordinated capacity-building, improved legal protection for women, strengthened gender equality mechanisms, and greater public awareness and engagement. The project aligns with national priorities, the 2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development - specifically SDGs 5, 16, and 17 and supports the implementation of Kazakhstan’s Family and Gender Policy Concept until 2030. It also contributes directly to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework 2026–2030, particularly Priority 1 on inclusive, accountable, and gender-responsive governance. 
The project’s Overall Goal (Impact) is to contribute to improved well-being for all people in Kazakhstan - especially the most vulnerable - through inclusive, effective, and accountable institutions that provide equal access to age- and gender-responsive, increasingly digitalised public and private services.

projects.description:
The outcome of Environmental Justice project is to promote a just recovery and sustainable development through accelerating preventive measures against environmental pollution. The project will strengthen responsible business practices in Kazakhstan and use of grievance mechanisms to restore violated rights of citizen and communities that experience environmental issues.

projects.name: Support to the national human rights mechanisms and the rule of law reforms in Kazakhstan
projects.description:
The project aims at enhancing the technical capacities and expertise of the key rule of law, security, and human rights institutions in Kazakhstan in response to the immediate needs spawned by the crisis in the country while contributing to announced political reforms of the government. The project has two key objectives:
First, the project targets to strengthen the national human rights mechanism institutionally. With the newly adopted law (December 2021) providing a Human Rights Commissioner (HRC) a more robust mandate and the expected uplift of HRC's status to the constitutional level, there is a need for immediate assistance to the NHRI in developing its capacity and strategic vision in fulfilling its new mandates.
Second, UNDP will work to support transformative changes in the work of law enforcement and, specifically, the police, towards people-centered, human rights-based services.

projects.name: Joint SDG Fund - Integrated Approaches for Digital Health Transformation in Kazakhstan
projects.description:
The project intends to use the requested seed funds to accelerate the digital transformation of the healthcare sector by 1) creating the gender-sensitive strategic vision and enabling effective coordination for the inclusive and sustainable development of digital health; 2) developing a favourable environment for efficient introduction and uptake of digital health interventions, and 3) leveraging investments in digital health through the development of the investment case, with a focus on most vulnerable populations.
The concrete expected results include 1) developed National Digital Health Strategy; 2) launched Secretariat on Digital Health serving as a hub for coordinating efforts, driving digitalization initiatives, and knowledge sharing; 3) conducted investment case to support evidence-based digital health policy-making based on cost-effectiveness analysis and return on investment on healthcare digitalization calculation; 4) improved capacities of national partners on health data analysis and secondary data use.

projects.name: Promoting the enhancement of protection policy
projects.description:
2022 UNHCR: As part of a working group on formulating the Migration Policy for 2023-27 and Social Code, UNHCR supported the Government by providing its technical expertise and recommendations for development of a Migration Policy for 2023-2027 and Social Code to enhance the national legal framework on asylum, refugee integration, extending their socio-economic rights including access to social protection services and allowance and facilitating naturalization. Bilateral meetings were conducted with line Ministries (MLSP, MoH, MoJ, MoEd), Members of the Parliament, Human Rights Ombudsman and other stakeholders, where the current situation of refugees and asylum-seekers in Kazakhstan, existing gaps in national legislation which hinder them from having effective access to social protection, employment, healthcare, education services, and necessary actions to be taken by the Government to promote and ensure the full realization of all human rights for all persons without discrimination in order to meet Kazakhstan’s obligations under international conventions were discussed. UNHCR recommendations were reflected in the Kazakhstan’s Human Rights action plan for 2022-2024. 
The refugee components were included in the 2nd Voluntary National Review (VNR) under SDG 10 “Granting access to basic socio-economic rights to refugees and asylum-seekers on an equal basis with permanently residing foreigners during their stay in Kazakhstan” and under SDG 16 “Ensuring the protection of the rights and interests of refugee and stateless children, ensuring security and access to social and educational services”. 
The situation of refugees in Kazakhstan along with challenges faced by them were submitted in the framework of UN Human Rights commissions (CERD and CAT) with recommendations to the Government of Kazakhstan to facilitate socio-economic integration and naturalization of refugees in line with international standards.

projects.name: Coordination of the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate all forms of HIV-related stigma and discrimination
projects.description:
In advancing the Global Partnership for Action to Eliminate HIV-Related Stigma and Discrimination in Kazakhstan, the UNAIDS Country Office demonstrated significant progress through the appointment of a national consultant to drive key initiatives. This consultant played a pivotal role in cultivating collaboration among diverse stakeholders, including the Kazakh Scientific Centre for Dermatology and Infection Diseases under the Ministry of Health, the People Living with HIV community, civil society partners, and national/international organizations. After supporting the process of drafting, UNAIDS facilitated multi-stakeholder meetings to track the implementation of the National Plan against Stigma and Discrimination related to HIV. The consultant's contributions were instrumental in bolstering AIDS service non-governmental organizations, particularly in areas such as advocacy for decriminalization of      HIV transmission/exposure and implementation of      the National Plan against Stigma and Discrimination related to HIV. Notably, in partnership with the Kazakhstan Union of People Living with HIV, the consultant facilitated      two pivotal meetings in Almaty and Astana, convening over 40 participants from AIDS Service NGOs, governmental structures, and national/international organizations. These meetings aimed to establish a unified position among civil society organizations regarding the decriminalization of HIV transmission at the country level, as well as gather support to advocacy from select state authorities, along with a number of preparatory meetings. Furthermore, the consultant played a crucial role in supporting AIDS Service NGOs in contributing to a UN confidential report for Kazakhstan's 2023 review by the Committee against Torture, demonstrating proactive involvement and a commitment to transparency and international cooperation.

Despite these steps, transgender individuals in Kazakhstan continue to face legal barriers, stigma, and discrimination, negatively impacting efforts to end the HIV epidemic. Notable legal obstacles include the prohibition of gender-affirming treatment until the age of 21, sterilization requirements for legal gender recognition, and others. Recognizing the urgency of addressing these challenges, the UNAIDS office played a central role in co-organizing a significant meeting focused on overcoming barriers to accessing HIV services for transgender people. This collaborative effort, in partnership with the Global Fund to Fight AIDS, TB and Malaria and AlmaTQ, a transgender civil society initiative, drew more than 40 participants, including representatives from NGOs, AIDS Centers, and national/international organizations. Discussions centered on addressing challenges related to HIV-associated stigma and human rights, raising awareness, and fostering collaboration among diverse stakeholders. Additionally, the UNAIDS office provided crucial support in enhancing the capacity of the transgender community to pursue strategic lawsuits with the newly established Constitutional Court of Kazakhstan, aimed at reviewing legal provisions discriminating against transgender people. As a direct outcome of these efforts, legislation concerning legal barriers for transgender people underwent comprehensive analysis, two cases were referred to the Constitutional Court, and notably, a comprehensive Transgender Community Advocacy Strategy for 2023-2026 was successfully developed. These accomplishments underscore the UNAIDS Country Office's unwavering commitment to creating a more inclusive and supportive environment for people affected by HIV-related stigma and discrimination in Kazakhstan.

The 'Let Communities Lead' regional leadership campaign commenced with a dynamic three-day communications training for 10 community leaders across six countries. Focused on honing public speaking and media interaction skills, participants crafted engaging content for the campaign's social media drive in Eastern Europe and Central Asia. Over 10 days, leaders were showcased on Twitter, Facebook, and Instagram, amassing a remarkable total reach exceeding 300,000 views. This success underscores the campaign's efficacy in galvanizing and motivating communities through strategic communication. UNAIDS Kazakhstan, a key contributor to the regional initiative, enriched the UNAIDS Global World AIDS Day campaign with a compelling video showcasing how community groups connect at-risk clients to PrEP in Kazakhstan.

This support was instrumental in the development of the approved HIV Road Map 2023-2026, which currently functions as a guiding document, effectively coordinating national efforts in HIV prevention and treatment.

As Kazakhstan endeavors to achieve the ambitious goal of eliminating AIDS as a public health threat by 2030, it becomes imperative to proactively plan for the continuation of HIV response achievements beyond the year 2025. To sustain these efforts and ensure adequate financial resources, Kazakhstan should prioritize the creation of Sustainability Roadmaps for the HIV Response within the next two years. This strategic planning will be crucial in maintaining momentum and ensuring a robust, enduring response to the HIV epidemic.

projects.name: Governments and partners have increased knowledge and capacity to develop and implement measures related to human mobility in the context of the environment and climate change.
projects.description:
The longitudinal study on human mobility in the context of climate change in the mountainous areas of the Almaty oblast in Kazakhstan demonstrated the complex and multifaceted impacts of environmental and climate hazards on households in the mountain areas. As per the research results, rising temperatures, earthquakes, blizzards, strong winds, and abnormal heat and cold conditions put pressure on the local population, affecting physical safety, water security, and mental well-being. Despite the difficult environmental conditions in the study area this year, residents prefer to stay in their communities.

 

IOM also developed the report on the “Mapping and analysis of basic legislation, policies and strategies in Kazakhstan in terms of the impact of the environment and climate change on migration processes”.

 

Evidence from the baseline survey and the mapping report will be discussed with relevant sectoral government entities in Kazakhstan. Evidence will also inform the formulation of the National Adaptation Plan

 

Capacity building:

 

Organized a regional capacity development workshop in Almaty in April 2024 for the representatives from the academic community and sectoral government entities. The methodology, survey tool, and study area were discussed during this workshop.
projects.outcome: Output 3.2.2: I Improved capacities of relevant public authorities for development and implementation of Climate and DRR policies in the urban and rural areas, with a focus on vulnerable groups.

projects.name: Conduct Central Asian Women Leaders Dialogue Forum (MFA VC 2023)
projects.description:
During reporting period, UN Women supported Central Asian Women's Dialogue chaired by government. Through joint initiatives, significant progress was achieved:
1. Subregional Cooperation: Over 84 representatives from various sectors, with 80% women and 20% men, strengthened subregional cooperation and deepened their understanding of Women, Peace, and Security (WPS) commitments within 2030 Agenda. Progress in realizing the WPS agenda in Central Asia was reported, and new opportunities for promoting WPS priorities were explored. A pivotal outcome was formulation of a Roadmap of Cooperation among Central Asian countries to implement the WPS agenda, expected to guide regional cooperation and address challenges faced by women in conflict zones.
2. Combating Domestic Violence: More than 130 representatives, with 90% women and 10% men, from legislative and executive bodies, international organizations, and NGOs, intensified partnerships and exchanged experiences in preventing and combating domestic violence. High-level meeting focused on effective strategies and sustainable solutions, resulting in enhanced legal frameworks and shared commitment to implementing joint solutions. The participants adopted a statement condemning gender-based violence, which will guide ongoing advocacy efforts in region and beyond.

projects.name: Provide technical assistance to 2022 VAWG survey conduction (preparation, data collection, data analysis and presentation of the results)
projects.description:
In 2021, technical assistance was provided to the Bureau of National Statistics to prepare for the 2022 VAWG survey in Kazakhstan. This assistance included two national consultations: one with governmental partners to discuss indicators on violence against women and girls, and another with non-governmental partners to prioritize areas for the survey. Recommendations gathered from these consultations informed the development of the survey's questionnaire and methodology.
Eight specialists from the Bureau of National Statistics received training on methodological issues related to the survey, facilitated by international and national consultants. Twelve weekly discussions further delved into data collection methodology, sampling, and questionnaire formats.
The methodology and data collection instruments were developed and refined during these sessions, culminating in the finalization and translation of the survey questionnaire into Kazakh. A pilot survey was planned to be conducted in the Almaty region from mid-October to the end of January.

Technical assistance provided to BNS on 2022 VAWG survey and 2024 MICS results dissemination - the data validated, analytical reports developed and launched to government.

projects.name: The City Experiment Fund
projects.description: CEF is a regional UNDP initiative funded by the Slovak Transformation Fund, supported by the Ministry of Finance of the Slovak Republic, and coordinated by the UNDP Istanbul Regional Hub (IRH) innovation team. The project is implemented in five cities—Stepanavan (Armenia), Almaty (Kazakhstan), Prizren (Kosovo), Pljevlja (Montenegro), and Skopje (North Macedonia). CEF applies systems thinking through a ‘portfolio’ approach to help these cities address complex urban challenges effectively. This approach recognizes that addressing "wicked problems" requires experimentation, continuous learning, and adaptive management rather than single, linear solutions. By working at the intersection of innovative methods and technologies, CEF seeks to address multifaceted urban issues such as the impacts of migration, climate change, and inequality.

projects.description: Occupational safety and health is pivotal for decent work. Occupational accidents and work-related diseases have a significant human, social and economic cost, which can be properly and effectively addressed and minimised only when all constituents and relevant stakeholders work together and commit to ensuring safe and healthy workplaces for all.  In these endeavours, the International Labour Organization (ILO) works closely with national constituents and provides technical assistance. Occupational safety and health is an essential and fundamental element of the world of work that undergoes critical changes under the imminent influence of AI and digitalization. projects.name: Supporting Local Self-Governance Reform in Kazakhstan
projects.description: In recent years, Kazakhstan has been carrying out active reforms in the field of local government and self-governance. The process of granting additional powers to local self-governance bodies took place in several stages, during which there was a transition from indirect elections of akims of rural districts through maslikhats to direct elections, which took place in 2021. Also, over the years, the population of rural districts began to take part in the consideration of program documents on the development of the local community and the discussion of actual issues of landscaping and public order. With the gradual introduction of the fourth level of the budget, the role of the population in solving local issues was strengthened, and the level of responsibility and competence of the akims of rural districts has increased. These measures have already had a positive impact and continue to contribute to increasing the transparency of the decision-making process by state bodies and the effective development of the local self-governance system. This project plans to: [i] raise awareness and knowledge of the akims of rural districts and local communities about the expansion of the functions of local governments and akims, mechanisms for direct financing of local budgets; [ii] promote the involvement of local communities in the decision-making process; [iii] obtain the necessary information and develop approaches and recommendations for further institutionalization of local self-governance in Kazakhstan.

projects.name: Provide technical and expert support for the establishment National Disaster Loss Database and its integration.
projects.description:
2021 narrative: UNDRR supported establishing the national system of disaster loss accounting. UNDRR facilitated establishing a TWG consisting of 50+ representatives of the central and regional departments of the Ministry of Emergency Situations and Oblast Akimats. In a series of workshops and consultative meetings, a customized data card aligned to national legislation and compatible with the global DesInventar-Sendai system was developed. UNDRR provided training for the TWG on the use of the DesInventar-Sendai international reporting system and shared the required software.
On July, 2022, specialists of Analytical units of all regional Departments of ES got refresher training on DesInventar-Sendai system. projects.name: Provide technical and expert support for increasing commitments of local authorities to build local-level resilience
projects.description:
2021 narrative: UNDRR is implementing community-based disaster risk activities with total coverage of 10,000 populations of 10 vulnerable communities in the East Kazakhstan region. In each of the target communities, emergency committees were formed and trained. One school and the local Akimat received the set of equipment - the emergency preparedness kit that included motorized pumps and electrical generators, flashlights, blankets, and many more. On September 20-23, 2021, UNDRR conducted a monitoring visit to 5 out 10 target communities. During the visit, UNDRR, IFRC, and RCS discussed with the local community representatives and mayors the local resilience strengthening activities and the small-scale mitigation projects aimed at reduction of vulnerability to seasonal floods and other hazards.

In 2022, UNDRR with the implementing partners Red Crescent of Kazakhstan and IFRC completed 4 small-scale mitigation projects in 3 communities of Altay and Glubokovskii rayons. Each of 10 target communities received a set of equipment for non-structural mitigation.

projects.name: Campaign to mobilize adolescent/teenagers, including teenagers living with HIV in Kazakhstan
projects.description: The UN's interventions prioritize the active involvement of marginalized groups, such as adolescents living with HIV. In Kazakhstan, UNAIDS empowers these adolescents through the Teenergizer movement, positioning them as leaders in the fight against HIV and advocates for youth rights. The project, implemented in hybrid format, includes face-to-face meetings in Almaty and online sessions in other regions. Weekly face-to-face meetings in Almaty enhance public speaking skills for 590 participants, while online sessions support 120 adolescents with HIV in improving public speaking and emotional intelligence. Additionally, 64 non-HIV interns engage in Teenergizer activities through internship courses. Teenergizer's impactful initiatives include video clips addressing HIV prevention and mental well-being, podcasts promoting tolerance, and advocacy efforts highlighting discriminatory legislation affecting PLHIV rights. Training sessions on HIV prevention, sexual health, substance use, and violence prevention reached 2392 participants through 59 sessions, with 34 trainings in Almaty and 25 in five regions of Kazakhstan. All media content and activities are accessible on the Teenergizer Instagram page and website.

projects.description: 2021 narrative: Follow-Up Study on Knowledge, Attitude and Practices on Violence Against Children in Families in Kazakhstan was completed and validated with national stakeholders. The findings were well received by the participants. The study identified both positive and negative trends: 7-percentage point decrease in general public support for the use of corporal punishment in the home and family, and a 10.1-percentage point decrease in child protection specialists support for the use of corporal punishment in families; 13.8-percentage point increase in general public understanding of mental violence and a 8.2-percentage point increase in child protection specialists understanding of mental violence; 3-percentage point increase in the proportion of parents/adults who reported using non-violent discipline.  The report is being prepared for public release.

projects.name: Advancing Water Science for Societies in Central Asia
projects.description: Central Asia (CA) is experiencing increasing water stress due to changing demand for water, population growth and demand for food security. Shared water resources in the region and the predicted impacts of climate change on the glacial sources of the major rivers, further exacerbate the challenges. Water is at the heart of the socio-economic development and SDG6 is pivotal for most of the other SDGs. Water cooperation is therefore an enabling factor for sustainable economic development and stability in the region. Improving water management is essential to meet the needs of the countries to achieve SDG6. The activity will address water security challenges in CA through advanced research, education, capacity building and cooperation among water experts, policy makers, communities and youth.

This project was focused on enhancing rural women's skills in cheese-making (link), hop cultivation (link), and felt needlework (link) in Kostanay, West-Kazakhstan, Mangystau, and Zhambyl oblasts, since these regions have big potential and are rich with raw materials for the development of entrepreneurship in these areas. Practical workshops and training, contributed women to balance unpaid housework with entrepreneurship, fostering economic independence and challenging gender stereotypes. This hands-on approach was crucial in ensuring the sustainability of the women's economic activities. Considering the social importance of the project UN Women gained support from key partners including the National Chamber of Entrepreneurs “Atameken”, and state sector entities to facilitate market access for the products developed by the beneficiaries of the training.

The expert review conducted, good practices in providing services to GBV survivors, including issues of PwD, and on SOPs use are shared. In total 123 ppl have been trained: 48 staff of CSPSs; 7 managers and staff of crisis centers; 68 ppl - staff of regional and district departments of public development, healthcare, social protection, police, education, psychologists, secretaries of commissions on women's affairs and family and demographic policy.

projects.description:
During the reporting period, UN Women continued to provide technical support to the government and the National Commission on Women Affairs and Family and Demographic Policy under the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan aimed at to ensure the effective integration of gender equality initiatives within various sectors of the government and society.

As a result, an inter-agency coordination was strengthened towards promoting and institutionalizing the country's commitments through joint work and cooperation of 17 representatives of the monitoring group comprising 89% women and 11% men from state and non-governmental sector organizations. On July 21, 2023, the expansion of existing commitments was initiated in joining the new Action Coalition for "Technology and Innovation for Gender Equality." The primary focus of this new coalition is to expand access to digital technologies, with the overarching goal of strengthening economic opportunities for women and girls. By joining the Action Coalition, Kazakhstan aims to foster an environment that not only empowers women in the digital realm but also ensures they have equal opportunities to contribute to and benefit from technological advancements.
