projects.name: Provide expert and technical support for effective implementation of the Concept for Family and Gender Policy in Kazakhstan (MFA VC).
projects.description:
UN Women continued to provide expert and technical support to the government of Kazakhstan towards the effective implementation of the Concept for Family and Gender Policy and contributed to the broader global agenda for gender equality and women's empowerment.

During the reporting period, the international community's awareness of gender policies in Kazakhstan and understanding of the country's commitment to addressing sexual violence was strengthened during a side event on "Practice of Application of the Istanbul Convention: Comprehensive Assistance to Victims of Sexual Violence" organized on June 1, 2023. This event, convened by the Permanent Mission of Kazakhstan and Belgium to the UN in Geneva, in collaboration with the Council of Europe served as a platform to further enhance the discussions around the possibilities of Kazakhstan’s potential accession to the Istanbul Convention.

In addition, UN Women's efforts also led to the reinforced collaborative environment, examination, and the exchange of experiences on various aspects of women's and girls' rights on the global stage during the 78th session of the General Assembly's third committees, held between October 1-20, 2023. The session provided a forum for comprehensive discussions on the advancement of women, elimination of discrimination, sexual and gender-based violence, and human rights frameworks. Attendees of the Third Committee of the General Assembly had the opportunity to engage with special rapporteurs, independent experts, and chairs of treaty bodies and working groups, as mandated by the Human Rights Council and the General Assembly.

projects.description:
In 2023 leadership skills of 24 women and girls living with HIV were elevated by UN Women through a 3-day Leadership School for women and girls living with HIV from the Karaganda and Pavlodar regions aiming to bolster knowledge, enhance abilities and skills, and foster a stronger sense of community among the attendees and provision of a space for meaningful engagement and mobilizing women leaders for joint action.
With UN Women’s support, 24 women living with HIV enhanced their knowledge of gender equality, feminism, human rights, leadership and the prevention and combat of gender-based violence. Through a series of structured sessions, these women strengthened their abilities to recognize and address discrimination on multiple grounds, and were equipped with essential knowledge and skills, ensuring they emerge as informed leaders and advocates within their communities. Furthermore, the Leadership School played a pivotal role in enhancing their abilities to effectively assess the unique challenges and needs faced by women living with HIV in Kazakhstan, thereby fostering a more informed and responsive community.

projects.name: Provide expert support and technical assistance to support the national eMTCT (elimination of mother to child transmission of HIV and other infections) TWG (technical working group) to finalize the process of obtaining validation of eMTCT for HIV and other diseases (eg syphilis) for Kazakhstan.
projects.description:
UNAIDS and WHO joined forces in a collaborative effort to develop an Action Plan aimed at fulfilling the objectives set forth by the WHO Euro Regional Commission on the elimination of mother-to-child transmission of HIV (eMTCT). This comprehensive initiative involved conducting 17 expert interviews and engaging the expertise of 45 specialists from six different regions. Furthermore, the collaboration extended its reach by actively involving HIV service organizations.

The discussions held as part of this initiative covered crucial aspects such as human rights, HIV-related stigma, and discrimination. In a concerted effort, the organizations compiled a wealth of information, encompassing over 80 documents in English. These documents, inclusive of updated indicators, provided a comprehensive overview of the activities related to eMTCT at both national and regional levels.

Subsequent to the WHO Euro Regional Commission Verification mission on eMTCT, numerous recommendations were generated for the Ministry of Health and the Kazakh Scientific Centre for Dermatology and Infectious Diseases. However, acknowledging the extensive time required for the implementation of these recommendations, the decision has been made to temporarily close this activity. It remains subject to potential reopening at a later date, subject upon changes in the country's landscape concerning the prevention of mother-to-child transmission of HIV

By joining forces with the Ministry of Education, the program gains access to valuable resources and an extensive network, further strengthening its potential impact. As part of the work plan, the training sessions are scheduled to be conducted in regions in 2024.

projects.name: Conduct a series of capacity-building training on the “Responsible and engaged fatherhood” Promote the “Men Engage” concept in the regions of Kazakhstan through two regions of Kazakhstan.
projects.description: In 2020 UNFPA finalized the package of training materials on Men Engage concept. Based on the developed materials 2 two-days ToTs were conducted: in Atyrau in April, 2023 and in Turkestan in June 2023. According to a comprehensive national sociological survey "The role of men, their level of engagement in family life and parenthood in Kazakhstan" that was conducted in 2021 with the support of UNFPA the needs of women with regard to the help of their spouses in the work about the house, in most cases, are not completely satisfied. A significant proportion of women do much more household chores than their spouses. Almost every fourth man (26%) does not agree with the statement "Women should have the same rights and opportunities as men." Among those who support the statement 35% are from the Atyrau region. Almost every fifth man (21%) agrees with the statement that "A woman must endure violence in order to keep her family save from the divorce”. Among the respondents who support this statement, 41% attributed themselves to a group of strongly religious men and most of them were from Turkestan (43%) and Atyrau regions (30%). Therefore, these 2 regions were chosen for the conduction of ToTs. Each ToT gathered 25 active men of different social positions: fathers, grandfathers, married men not married, men working in NGOs and etc. In total 50 men were trained.

projects.name: Phase 1. Climate Promise Kazakhstan – From Pledge to Impact
projects.description:
This Project Initiation Plan is part of the global UNDP’s flagship initiative, the Climate Promise: From Pledge to Impact - Leveraging the Climate Promise to turn enhanced Nationally Determined Contributions (eNDC) into ambitious climate action.
The project has been initiated as a response to the country's request for NDC Partnership. This project aims to support national efforts to reduce greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions and achieve carbon neutrality by 2060, aligning with commitments such as the Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) and the Carbon Neutral Strategy. It involves developing a comprehensive tool and methodology to evaluate the impact of national programs and policies on GHG emissions, as well as building capacity among stakeholders to effectively use these tools.
The project also focuses on establishing measurable emission reduction outcomes, including long-term targets and interim milestones for key sectors. Sector-specific reduction pathways will be developed based on projections and scenarios, identifying programs and projects that can contribute to emissions reduction. Additionally, the project includes a social and gender impact assessment of the Carbon Neutral Strategy to ensure an equitable transition, along with the development of legislation and regulations to strengthen waste management practices and reduce sectoral emissions.

projects.name: Develop recommendations for the advancing of women's entrepreneurship in the field of art and culture through gender analysis of barriers and implementation of legal acts.
projects.description: In Kazakhstan, the creative sector has long been an underexplored avenue for women's economic empowerment. Recognizing this potential, UN Women, in collaboration with partners, embarked on an initiative to transform the lives of women artists through a series of seminars on the Creative Economy. Through this initiative, over 80 women creative professionals from all regions of Kazakhstan strengthened their potential and gained skills in placing their piece of art in international and national marketplaces and monetizing them. The seminars, were designed as a first step towards integrating creative professionals from various regions of Kazakhstan Initially, the results were modest, as understanding and mastering the aspects of entering this dynamic sector is a long-term endeavor. As the result of consultative work with national partners artists were included in the State's Cultural Policy Concept, and the field of Art (OKED 90.300 – General Economic Activity Classifier) was incorporated into the Creative Economy's OKED classifier. These developments marked a significant recognition and integration of the arts into the broader economic narrative of Kazakhstan. The recognition of artists in the Cultural Policy Concept and the inclusion of Art in the Creative Economy classifier were significant external factors that validated and supported the program's objectives.

projects.name: Support to livelihoods and integration of women and vulnerable households through small business development programs
projects.description:
IOM Kazakhstan completed a three-month vocational training in tailoring (sewing), manicure-pedicure, hair dress stylist, SMM and Kazakh language courses in partnership with a local NGO for 440 female and 60 male Afghan beneficiaries, at the VET centres in Shymkent and Almaty. The vocational training has been offered based on the results of needs assessment of the Afghan population in two regions of Kazakhstan. Upon the completion of the VET courses, each of the 500 beneficiaries were given equipment, such as a tailoring machine, hairdresser stylist machine, tablets and manicure-pedicure tools. Following the successful completion of these VET courses, IOM Kazakhstan initiated and conducted numerous meetings with private sector representatives such a private City Hotel in Shymkent and Atameken chamber of entrepreneurs of Kazakhstan, to discuss entrepreneurship. During the meetings, questions of cooperation and employment of Afghan beneficiaries were raised, and it was agreed that there were potential employment opportunities on offer for beneficiaries to work in tailoring. City hotel warmly greeted IOM’s initiatives and expressed its intention to support this activity going forward.
IOM Kazakhstan worked on a Fashion week event due to take place in Autumn 2024 and has already selected the Service Provider for executing this activity. This event will contribute to the social wellbeing of beneficiaries and represents a huge opportunity for them to show their potential in the tailoring and sewing industry, including their view of beauty and design. This event should open new pathways for Afghan women involved in the fashion and beauty industry of Kazakhstan

projects.name: Provide expert support and technical assistance for strengthened coordination and cooperation with international communities and the government (internal and extended Gender Theme Groups)
projects.description:
During the third and fourth quarters of 2023, the Extended Gender Theme Group (EGTG) conducted two significant meetings, bringing together key stakeholders to address gender-related issues and promote inclusivity. The co-chairs of the EGTG included the Deputy Head of the National Commission for Women, Family, and Demographic Policy under the President of the Republic of Kazakhstan, the Deputy Head of Mission of the Kingdom of the Netherlands to Central Asia, and the United Nations Resident Coordinator for Kazakhstan, who later delegated the role to the UN Women Representative. The active participation of the Government of Kazakhstan, along with representatives from various Ministries, Diplomatic Missions, and international organizations, marked a collaborative and inclusive approach to the group's mission.

The EGTG meetings witnessed the active engagement of the Government of Kazakhstan, with representatives from the Ministries of Foreign Affairs, Constitution Court, Ombudsperson for Human Rights, and other relevant entities. Furthermore, over 20 Diplomatic Missions in Kazakhstan, including Embassies of Austria, Belgium, Canada, Egypt, Finland, France, Germany, Jordan, Latvia, the Netherlands, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, the Slovak Republic, UK, and US actively participated. International organizations and IFIs were well-represented by ADB, EBRD, EU Delegation, OSCE, USAID, and various UN entities.

The meeting on 20 September primarily focused on planning for the 2023 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence (GBV) campaign.
The meeting on 13 December centered on two key aspects: Reflections on the Impact of the 16 Days of Activism Against Gender-Based Violence 2023 and Embassy Experiences, specifically focusing on engaging youth across Kazakhstan on GBV.
An internal GTG meeting was held on 5 October in a hybrid format, discussing various pertinent themes:

UNDP presented their STEM Initiative.
Joint initiatives in the framework of the "16 Days of Activism against Gender-Based Violence" Campaign 2023 were discussed.
UNCT SWAP Gender Score Card Assessment update was presented.
The development of the GTG Newsletter for Q4-2023-Q1-2024 was discussed.
The Extended Gender Theme Group meetings served as valuable platforms for collaboration, knowledge sharing, and strategic planning. The commitment of the group to promoting gender equality, addressing intersectional issues, and fostering inclusive societies was evident in the depth of discussions and the diversity of perspectives represented. The participation of Diplomatic Missions, international organizations, and IFIs underscored the importance of a multi-stakeholder approach in achieving gender-related goals.

projects.name: Conduct monitoring visits to the regions.
projects.description:
During the reporting period, the UN Women Project team conducted three monitoring visits to oversee and evaluate the implementation of project activities. These monitoring visits were specifically focused on the regions of Kostanay, Mangistau, and West Kazakhstan. The primary objective of these visits was to assess the progress of entrepreneurship training initiatives targeted at vulnerable women, with a particular emphasis on practical skill development.

The primary goal of the monitoring visits was to assess the on-the-ground implementation of project activities related to entrepreneurship training for vulnerable women.

The project team sought to gather feedback from participants, trainers, and local partners to gain insights into the impact of the training and identify areas for improvement.

The three monitoring visits conducted by the UN Women Project team during the reporting period underscore the commitment to ensuring the successful implementation of entrepreneurship training activities for vulnerable women. By assessing the on-the-ground realities in Kostanay, Mangistau, and West Kazakhstan, UN Women is better positioned to refine strategies, address challenges, and maximize the positive impact of the project on the economic empowerment of vulnerable women in these regions.

projects.name: Assisting Kazakhstan in the implementation of the Concept of family and gender policy in terms of gender equality and empowerment of all women and girls in KZ and overcoming the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic crisis
projects.description: The project "Assisting Kazakhstan in the implementation of the Concept of family and gender policy in terms of gender equality and empowerment of all women and girls in Kazakhstan and overcoming the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic crisis" has the overall objective of providing effective and timely support to the Government of the Republic of Kazakhstan to achieve gender equality and empower all women and girls in Kazakhstan. This includes the most vulnerable groups and takes into account the consequences of the COVID-19 pandemic crisis. The joint project is implemented by UN Women, UNFPA and UNESCO until 2024. UNESCO has the following activities under this project: 1) Conducting a comprehensive analysis of national education policies and programs based on the UNESCO Gender in Education Toolkit to promote gender equality in and through education 2) Conducting anti-discrimination and gender-lensed expertise of educational materials to identify negative gender and/ or other biases and prejudices in order to provide specific recommendations and proposals for mainstreaming gender equality in the curricula and methodologies 3) Developing training programme for teachers and educators in instilling key competencies and skills for mainstreaming gender equality in and through education, as well as promote the teaching of a culture of equality and non-discrimination at all levels of education. 4) Training of teachers and educators in instilling key competencies and skills for mainstreaming gender equality in and through education, as well as promote the teaching of a culture of equality and non-discrimination at all levels of education.
